50757952.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to wild type human biotin labelled p38 alpha (9 to 352 residues) expressed in sf21 insect cells SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) experiments were performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. The wild type human biotin labelled p38α (9 to 352 residues) expressed in sf21 insect cells was immobilized on a streptavidin-coated sensor chip (SA) at a density of 1000–1500 RU. The inhibitors were diluted in HBS-EP buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 3 mM EDTA, 0.005% P20) and injected at concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 100 nM at a flow rate of 30 μL/min. The association phase lasted 120 s, followed by a dissociation phase of 300 s. The sensor surface was regenerated with 10 mM glycine-HCl (pH 2.0) for 30 s. Data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The equilibrium dissociation constants (KD) were determined by fitting the sensorgrams to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model. The association (kon) and dissociation (koff) rate constants were calculated from the fitted curves. The residence time (τ) was calculated as τ = 1/koff. The half-life (t1/2) was calculated as t1/2 = ln(2)/koff.

50758132.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to wild type human biotin labelled p38 alpha (9 to 352 residues) expressed in sf21 insect cells assessed as dissociation rate constant by SPR analysis
50758132.references_previous: Reference 55: Willemse-Seegers, N.; Uitdehaag, J. C.; Manning, M. B.; de Vetter, J. R.; de Man, J.; Sawa, M.; Kawase, Y.; Buijsman, R. C.; Zaman, G. J. Compound selectivity and target residence time of kinase inhibitors studied with surface plasmon resonance. J. Mol. Biol. 2017, 429, 574–586.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Binding Kinetics. The kinetic constants of the aforementioned selected p38α MAP kinase inhibitors were determined by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) measurement (Table 7) to investigate the impact of type I1/2 inhibition on a compound’s binding kinetics.55 Equilibrium dissociation constants (KD) were determined by measuring the association (ka) and dissociation rates (kd) of the individual compounds and binding affinities in the low nanomolar range (1.3–43.5 nM) were obtained. The inhibitors selected from our synthesized library were tested against a small panel of reference compounds consisting of literature-described type I and type II p38α MAP kinase inhibitors. 13b, a prototypical type II inhibitor, showed the lowest KD with 0.123 nM. 3-(3-Bromo-4-((2,4-difluorobenzyl)oxy)-6-methyl-2-oxopyridin-1(2H)-yl)-N,4-dimethylbenzamide 13d (PH-79780456), a type I inhibitor and clinical candidate from Pfizer, had an affinity (2.5 nM) similar to most of the dibenzosuberone and dibenzoepinone compounds. Comparing the TRTs of the reference inhibitors with our type I1/2 series showed an improved TRT of the dibenzosuberones 6b, 6e, 6g, 6j, 6l, and 8b (τ = 259–3660 s) compared to the classical type I inhibitors such as 13d (τ = 36 s) and 13a (τ = 4.6 s). The longest TRTs in the dibenzosuberone series were observed for compounds containing an additional fluorine group at position 2 (e.g., 8b and 8e). Worthy of note is that the improved TRT of this series correlated with a high potency in the human whole blood cellular assay (8b, IC50 = 31 nM; 8e, IC50 = 34 nM). The dibenzoepinone series generally showed a less pronounced improvement in TRT. However, an important exception to this trend was observed regarding 6q, which showed the highest TRT among all tested inhibitors (τ = 4099 s).

immobilization.ligand_name: wild type human biotin labelled p38 alpha (9 to 352 residues)

analyte.description: p38α MAP kinase inhibitors (including synthesized compounds and reference inhibitors such as 13b, 13d, 6b, 6e, 6g, 6j, 6l, 8b, 6q)
